title: The Wrong Portrait Revisited
premise: Folklorist Sebastian Almeida arrives in the dying village of Hollowmere to record its songs before the last resident, old Mrs. Vane, sells the estate to developers. His sleep recordings begin capturing a second voice that answers questions he never asked aloud—a voice that knows the village's drowned history and demands he learn the folk song's missing last verse. As Sebastian documents the haunting, he realizes the song was a binding contract: the verse was cut away to imprison something beneath the manor, and his recordings are feeding it memory. In the end, Sebastian must choose between destroying his archive to silence the thing forever or singing the final verse himself to inherit its power—choosing the latter, he becomes Hollowmere's last resident, the new keeper the papers were always meant to bind.
about_author: Quentin Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in coastal villages before turning to fiction. They live alone with a reel-to-reel recorder they refuse to plug in.

chapters.title: The Village That Sings Once
chapters.summary: Sebastian Almeida arrives in Hollowmere, notebook and recorder in hand, and is met with polite silence: every villager will sing a song for him exactly once, then refuse to repeat it. POV Sebastian. Beat: unease masked as professional excitement—the first crack in his faith that documentation is harmless.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vane's Papers
chapters.summary: Sebastian meets Edith Vane, the last resident of the manor, who is being pressured to sign sale papers by a slick developer's agent. She agrees to let him record her songs if he stays through the equinox. POV Sebastian. Beat: wary alliance; the reader senses she is testing him for something.

chapters.title: The Drowned Verse
chapters.summary: Edith sings 'The Laying Song,' but stops before a final verse, claiming she never learned it. The village archive confirms every version ends at the same broken line. POV Sebastian. Beat: scholarly obsession kindles; a mystery with teeth.

chapters.title: What the Night Recorder Keeps
chapters.summary: Sebastian leaves his recorder running while he sleeps. Playback reveals hours of him talking—and a second voice, low and patient, answering questions he never asked. POV Sebastian. Beat: dread; his own bedroom becomes untrustworthy territory.

chapters.title: Interview with a Static
chapters.summary: Sebastian experiments, asking questions aloud before sleeping; the voice answers on tape, describing a flood, a bargain, and 'the one who keeps the ledger.' POV Sebastian. Beat: compulsion—he starts treating the haunting as a research subject, a fatal professional habit.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Following the voice's clues, Sebastian finds a hidden ledger in the manor listing every villager's name beside a sung line—documentation as contract. His own name is already entered, in fresh ink. POV Sebastian, with a brief Edith interlude. Beat: violation; the archive has been writing back.

chapters.title: Villagers Who Remember Wrong
chapters.summary: Sebastian interviews villagers and finds their memories of the flood contradict the ledger; one old man weeps at a name he insists he never had. POV Sebastian. Beat: creeping horror that memory itself is being edited by the thing below.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession, Half Sung
chapters.summary: Edith admits her family cut the song's last verse generations ago to bind something in the well beneath the manor; the sale papers are actually a transfer of the binding. She begs him to leave before the equinox. POV Edith. Beat: tragic guilt; the mentor figure withholds the worst.

chapters.title: The Developer's Signature
chapters.summary: The agent, Corven, reveals he knows exactly what the papers are and wants the power beneath, not the land; he has been buying failing villages like this for years. POV Sebastian. Beat: human villain surfaces—greed as a rival haunting.

chapters.title: Songs Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Villagers begin singing their songs a second time involuntarily, in their sleep, in unison across the village; each repetition weakens the binding. POV Sebastian. Beat: escalation; the whole village becomes an instrument being played.

chapters.title: The Voice Learns My Name
chapters.summary: The second voice starts using Sebastian's name and describing his childhood; it claims his recordings have given it his memories to wear. POV Sebastian. Beat: intimate terror; the archive has become a doorway into him.

chapters.title: Corven's First Attempt
chapters.summary: Corven breaks into the manor to force Edith's signature; the well-thing defends its prison, nearly killing him, and Sebastian saves Corven—binding them in uneasy alliance of necessity. POV Sebastian. Beat: moral complexity; saving a predator.

chapters.title: The First Verse, Remembered
chapters.summary: Decoding the ledger, Sebastian realizes the song's verses are instructions for the binding—and that the missing verse is the release clause. He begins reconstructing it from fragment recordings. POV Sebastian. Beat: dark scholarship; knowledge as contamination.

chapters.title: Edith Fades
chapters.summary: Edith's memories dissolve as the thing feeds; she forgets Sebastian between visits, then her own marriage, then her name. POV Edith. Beat: heartbreak; inheritance as erosion, the last keeper being erased before she can sign.

chapters.title: The Equinox Rehearsal
chapters.summary: On the equinox eve, the village sleep-sings the whole song but the last verse, and the ground beneath the manor answers in harmony. Sebastian records it and hears his own voice in the chorus. POV Sebastian. Beat: peak dread; he is already part of the pattern.

chapters.title: Corven's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corven offers to destroy Sebastian's archive in exchange for the reconstructed verse, intending to sing it himself and take the power. Sebastian refuses—and Corven steals the ledger pages. POV Sebastian. Beat: betrayal; the scholar's work weaponized.

chapters.title: What the Archive Prays To
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts the truth that his documentation has been feeding the entity memory and strength; every recording was a prayer answered by the wrong listener. POV Sebastian. Beat: guilt and reckoning; his identity as archivist collapses.

chapters.title: Edith Signs
chapters.summary: Dying and half-erased, Edith signs the papers—not selling to Corven but willing the keeping to Sebastian, the only name the ledger will accept. She dies at dawn, finally remembering everything at the end. POV Edith. Beat: sacrificial passing of the burden; grief.

chapters.title: The Verse Sung Wrong
chapters.summary: Corven sings the reconstructed verse at the well, but omits the ledger's final line; the entity takes him instead of obeying him, and his scream joins the village's sleep-chorus. POV Sebastian, witnessing. Beat: climax begins; power devours the corrupt.

chapters.title: The Last Verse Without Singing
chapters.summary: Sebastian descends to the well and learns the true last verse by reading it silently—the one way to complete the binding without joining the song. The entity offers him power if he sings; he holds the silence. POV Sebastian. Beat: climax; willpower against temptation, memory against erasure.

chapters.title: The New Keeper
chapters.summary: Sebastian completes the binding and burns his archive, but the ledger rewrites itself with his name as keeper; the voice goes quiet, waiting, patient. He stays in Hollowmere as its last resident. POV Sebastian. Beat: pyrrhic victory; inheritance fulfilled in the worst way.

chapters.title: A Song Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Years later, a young folklorist arrives in Hollowmere and Sebastian, keeper now, sings her a song—once. That night her recorder catches a second voice. POV the newcomer, closing on Sebastian listening. Beat: cyclical dread; the archive prays on.
